dream: I walked on the cool card and found the wide anchor there, heavy and flat like a drawing. I pressed it down on a tired wedge that felt too thin to bite. The card hummed forty-four, a low hum that sounded like the air was wet paper. I pressed the wide rock until my hands cramped, hoping to stop the slip from sliding into the tall, tall i I had built. The stand felt round and wrong, crowding the flat shapes I trusted. I woke inside the dream, the wide anchor still lying flat, waiting for a slide that would never come.
